question: Counting accidents and pollution, which kills the most people per unit of electricity: coal, gas, hydropower or nuclear?
answer: Coal, by far: about 25 deaths per terawatt-hour, mostly from the air pollution it causes, against 0.03 for nuclear, Chernobyl and Fukushima included. A nuclear accident is sudden, visible and named; coal's toll is spread thin, a few deaths in every city every year. A terawatt-hour is about a year's electricity for 150,000 Europeans.
move: Deaths in one place make news; deaths spread everywhere make only statistics.
source: Markandya & Wilkinson, Lancet, 2007; Our World in Data
reference: Markandya, A. & Wilkinson, P. (2007) Electricity generation and health, The Lancet 370: 979-990; Ritchie, H. (2020) What are the safest and cleanest sources of energy? Our World in Data
ask: Which energy source frightens me most, and how many deaths per unit of power does it cause?

items.label: Nuclear
items.note: Chernobyl and Fukushima included: about 800 times safer than coal.

items.label: Hydropower
items.note: Mostly one dam failure, Banqiao in China in 1975.

items.label: Coal
items.note: Almost all from air pollution: a slow toll nobody reports as a disaster.

items.label: Gas
items.note: It burns cleaner than coal: about a ninth of the deaths.
